cryptohome: Fix error code on non-existing chall-resp mount Return CRYPTOHOME_ERROR_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND from MountEx requests of KEY_TYPE_CHALLENGE_RESPONSE when the home directory doesn't exist and the request doesn't have the |create| field. This is important, since Chrome, even when signing the user in for the first time on the device, sends the first MountEx *without* the |create| field. Chrome then repeats this request *with* the |create| field, but only if the first request returned the non-fatal CRYPTOHOME_ERROR_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND error. This CL simply aligns the cryptohomed's challenge-response mount behavior with the existing and correct password-based mount behavior. BUG=chromium:842791 TEST=tast run $IP hwsec.ChallengeResponseMount Change-Id: Iaacafc575a16b127171dad811548a57b27436748 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1678657 Tested-by: Maksim Ivanov <emaxx@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Maksim Ivanov <emaxx@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Ryo Hashimoto <hashimoto@chromium.org>

arc: networkd: Play Services connectivity fix hack. https://crrev.com/c/1631854 changed from using signals to messages over unix sockets to indicate when ARC++ was starting up and shutting down. The upstart script used socat to send these messages. Occasionally, it appears socat cannot be found by the script shell. This patch restores partial preceding functionality by reverting back to pkill and having the manager construct the proper notification for broadcast to the child processes. This is a temporary workaround until the script itself is eliminated entirely (b:136050424). BUG=b:136049825 TEST=Flashed nocturne, manually logged in/out of ARC++, installed/ removed Play Store via settings dialog. Verified connectivity was intact.
